kinds.a: bacalhau · bacalao · baccalà · klippfisk · morue salée
kinds.d: Cod preserved by salting and drying, sold to be soaked and cooked.

x.n: Bacalhau de Cura Tradicional Portuguesa TSG
x.d: Portuguese traditional-cure salt cod protected as a TSG; graded by weight from Especial over 4 kg to Miúdo under 500 g.
x.dt: TSG protects the method, not the origin of the fish

kinds.d: Unsalted cod air-dried on racks for about three months, the base of lutefisk.

x.d: Skrei landed in Lofoten or Vesterålen and air-dried in Lofoten; Norwegian protection 2007, EU PGI 2014, the first Norwegian EU-certified product.
x.dt: over 20 quality grades · about 75% water lost

kinds.a: matjes · maatjes · Hollandse Nieuwe · salt herring
kinds.d: Herring cured in brine or salt and sold chilled, to be eaten as the fish itself.

x.d: Matjes herring from Glückstadt, Schleswig-Holstein, with PGI status.
x.dt: brined about five days in oak casks

x.d: Dutch new herring, a mild matjes from immature fish; Hollandse Nieuwe, Holländischer Matjes and Hollandse maatjesharing are EU TSGs.
x.dt: caught late May to early July at over 15% oil

kinds.d: Tuna loin salted and air-dried, sold whole or sliced; protected regional makes such as Mojama de Barbate are included.

x.d: Salt-cured wild tuna loin from the Gulf of Cádiz coast, from yellowfin or bluefin over 200 kg.
x.dt: Extra from the lean loin near the spine · Primera from the fattier outer loin

x.d: Mojama made in Barbate and La Janda, Cádiz, to the same tuna and grade rules.

kinds.d: Whole fish preserved by controlled fermentation and eaten as the fish itself, not as a paste or sauce.

x.d: Lightly salted Baltic herring from northern Sweden that goes on fermenting in the sealed tin; sales open on the third Thursday of August.
x.dt: canned from early July · tin bulges

x.d: Japanese freshwater fish packed in salt and rice and fermented for years.
Pungent salted and dried fish of the Izu Islands with a strong smell but mild flavour.

kinds.a: jeotgal · shiokara · bagoong · pla ra · saeujeot
kinds.d: Whole or cut seafood preserved by salting and fermenting and eaten as the seafood itself; a paste or sauce is in Pantry Staples.

x.d: Korean salted, fermented seafood, solid side dishes or the liquid aekjeot used in kimchi.
Philippine salted fish or shrimp paste fermented 30 to 90 days.
Japanese salted and fermented seafood, kept in the shape of the fish or as paste.

traditions.r: Portugal, with fish from Norway and Iceland
traditions.d: Dry-salted cod, a Portuguese staple adopted from Basque salting off Newfoundland.
traditions.auth: TSG label Bacalhau de Cura Tradicional Portuguesa

traditions.d: Skrei hung to dry outdoors for about three months, Norway's oldest food export still traded.
traditions.tech: open-air racks, cold wind, then sorting into 20-plus grades

traditions.d: Baltic herring brined then canned to ferment further, sold from the third Thursday of August.
traditions.tech: caught May and June, brined, headed and gutted, barrelled at 15 to 18 C, canned early July
